notes: # HTML - HTML is the standard markup language used to create and structure web pages. - It defines the content and layout of a webpage using tags and elements. - Features of HTML: easy to learn and use, platform independent, used to create web pages, supports images, links, tables, forms, and multimedia. - Works with CSS and JavaScript. - Basic Structure of an HTML Document: - - - - - <body> - HTML uses tags enclosed within angle brackets < >. - Common HTML Tags: - Heading Tags: <h1>, <h2>, <h3> - Paragraph Tag: <p> - Line Break Tag: <br> - Horizontal Rule: <hr> - Hyperlinks: used to link one page to another, syntax: <a href="https://www.google.com"> - Images: used to display images, syntax: <img src="image.jpg"> - Lists: - Ordered List: <ol> - Unordered List: <ul> - Tables: used to display data in a tabular format, example: <table border="1"> - Forms: used to collect user input, example: <form> - Text Formatting Tags: - Bold: <b> - Italic: <i> - Underline: <u> - HTML Attributes: provide additional information about elements, example: <a href="https://www.google.com"> - HTML5 Features: - Audio support - Video support - Canvas - Semantic elements - Local storage - Semantic Tags: - <header> - <nav> - <section> - <article> - <footer> - Advantages of HTML: - Simple and easy to learn - Free and open standard - Supported by all browsers - Creates structured web pages - Integrates with CSS and JavaScript

# DHTML

- DHTML is a combination of HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and DOM used to create dynamic and interactive web pages.
- It allows webpage content and appearance to change without reloading the page.
- Components of DHTML:
  - HTML: Provides the structure of the webpage.
  - CSS: Provides styling and layout.
  - JavaScript: Adds interactivity and dynamic behavior.
  - DOM (Document Object Model): Allows JavaScript to access and modify HTML elements.
- Features of DHTML:
  - Dynamic content updates.
  - Interactive web pages.
  - Event handling support.
  - Animation effects.
  - Real-time page modifications.
  - No page reload required for changes.
- Example of DHTML:
  - HTML code with JavaScript function to change text on button click.
- Event Handling in DHTML:
  - DHTML responds to user actions called events.
  - Common Events: onclick, onmouseover, onmouseout, onchange, onload.
- Applications of DHTML:
  - Interactive websites.
  - Online forms.
  - Menus and navigation bars.
  - Animations.
  - Games.
  - E-commerce websites.
- HTML vs DHTML:
  - HTML: Static web pages, content does not change automatically, no interactivity.
  - DHTML: Dynamic web pages, content can change dynamically, supports interactivity.
- Advantages of DHTML:
  - Improves user experience.
  - Creates interactive web pages.
  - Reduces page reloads.
  - Supports animations and effects.
  - Faster and more responsive interfaces.
- Disadvantages of DHTML:
  - More complex than HTML.
  - Browser compatibility issues may occur.
  - Requires knowledge of JavaScript and CSS.
- Exam Point:
  - DHTML is a technology that combines HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and DOM to create dynamic and interactive web pages.

# CSS

- CSS (Cascading Style Sheets) is a stylesheet language used to control the presentation, layout, and appearance of HTML documents.
- Advantages of CSS: 
  - Separates content from presentation
  - Improves webpage appearance
  - Reduces code repetition
  - Faster website maintenance
  - Supports responsive web design
- Basic Syntax: 
  - CSS
    1. selector
    2. {
    3. property: value;
    4. }
- Ways to Apply CSS:
  - Inline CSS: Applied directly inside an HTML tag
  - Internal CSS: Written inside the <style> tag in the HTML document
  - External CSS: Stored in a separate .css file
- CSS Selectors:
  - Element Selector: Applies to all elements
  - ID Selector: Uses # and applies to a specific element
  - Class Selector: Uses . and applies to multiple elements
- Common CSS Properties:
  - Text Color
  - Background Color
  - Font Size
  - Text Alignment
  - Border
- Box Model: Every HTML element is treated as a box consisting of Content, Padding, Border, and Margin
- CSS Positioning:
  - Static: Default position
  - Relative: Positions an element relative to its normal position
  - Absolute: Positions an element relative to its nearest positioned ancestor
  - Fixed: Positions an element relative to the viewport
- CSS List Styling: Used to style lists
- CSS Table Styling: Used to style tables
- CSS Pseudo Classes: Used to style elements based on user interactions
- Applications of CSS:
  - Website design
  - Responsive web pages
  - Mobile-friendly layouts
  - Animations and effects
  - User interface development

# XML

- XML is a markup language used to store, organize, and transport data in a structured format.
- Unlike HTML, XML is designed to store and exchange data, not to display it.
- Features of XML:
  - User-defined tags
  - Platform independent
  - Self-descriptive
  - Easy to read and write
  - Supports data exchange between applications
  - Extensible and flexible
- Basic Structure of XML Document:
  - <?xml version="1.0"?>
  - <root element>
    - <child element1>
    - <child element2>
    - ...
  - </root element>
- XML Elements:
  - Consist of a start tag, content, and end tag
  - Example: <name>John</name>
- XML Tags:
  - Are user-defined
  - Example: <book>
- XML Attributes:
  - Provide additional information about elements
  - Syntax: <element attribute="value">
  - Example: <student id="101">
- XML Tree Structure:
  - Represents the hierarchical organization of elements
  - Example: <college><student><name>John</name></student></college>
- XML Rules:
  - Must have a single root element
  - Tags must be properly closed
  - Tags are case-sensitive
  - Attribute values must be enclosed in quotes
  - Elements must be properly nested
- XML vs HTML:
  - XML: used for storing data, user-defined tags, extensible
  - HTML: used for displaying data, predefined tags, fixed tag set
- Advantages of XML:
  - Easy data sharing
  - Platform independent
  - Human-readable format
  - Supports structured data storage
  - Widely used in web services
- Applications of XML:
  - Data exchange between systems
  - Web services
  - Configuration files
  - Database applications
  - E-commerce systems
- Example XML Document:
  - <?xml version="1.0"?>
  - <employees>
    - <employee>
      - <id>1</id>
      - <name>Alice</name>
      - <salary>50000</salary>
    - </employee>
    - <employee>
      - <id>2</id>
      - <name>Bob</name>
      - <salary>60000</salary>
    - </employee>
  - </employees>

# Scripting

- Scripting is the process of writing interpreted programs called scripts to automate tasks and create dynamic applications.
- Scripting languages include JavaScript, Python, PHP, Perl, and Bash.
- Scripting is usually executed by an interpreter rather than being compiled into machine code.
- Features of Scripting Languages:
  - Easy to learn and write.
  - Interpreted execution.
  - Rapid development.
  - Portable across platforms.
  - Used for automation and web development.
- Types of Scripting:
  - Client-Side Scripting: Executed on the user's browser.
  - Server-Side Scripting: Executed on the web server.
- Advantages of Scripting:
  - Faster execution.
  - Reduces server load.
  - Improves user interaction.
  - Better security.
  - Access to databases.
  - Dynamic content generation.
- Scripting vs Programming:
  - Scripting: Usually interpreted, faster development, used for automation.
  - Programming: Usually compiled, more complex development, used for full applications.
- Applications of Scripting:
  - Web development.
  - Task automation.
  - System administration.
  - Data processing.
  - Game development.
  - Testing and deployment.
- Disadvantages of Scripting:
  - Generally slower than compiled programs.
  - Less efficient for large applications.
  - Security risks if poorly written.

# java Script

- JavaScript is a high-level, interpreted scripting language used to create dynamic and interactive web pages.
- It is one of the core technologies of web development along with HTML and CSS.
- Features of JavaScript:
  - Interpreted language.
  - Object-oriented.
  - Platform independent.
  - Event-driven.
  - Dynamic typing.
  - Supports client-side and server-side programming.
- Uses of JavaScript:
  - Form validation
  - Web page interactivity
  - Animations
  - Games
  - Web applications
  - Server-side development (Node.js)
- Adding JavaScript to HTML:
  - Internal JavaScript: <script> document.write("Hello JavaScript"); </script>
  - External JavaScript: app.js, <script src="app.js"></script>
- Variables:
  - Store data values.
  - Syntax: let age = 20; const PI = 3.14; var name = "John";
- Data Types:
  - Number: let x = 10;
  - String: let name = "John";
  - Boolean: let result = true;
  - Undefined: let value;
  - Null: let data = null;
- Operators:
  - Arithmetic Operators: +, -, *, /, %
  - Relational Operators: ==, !=, >, <, >=, <=
  - Logical Operators: &&, ||, !
- Conditional Statements:
  - if Statement: if(age >= 18) { console.log("Eligible"); }
  - if-else Statement: if(age >= 18) { console.log("Adult"); } else { console.log("Minor"); }
- Loops:
  - for Loop: for(let i = 1; i <= 5; i++) { console.log(i); }
  - while Loop: let i = 1; while(i <= 5) { console.log(i); i++; }
- Functions:
  - Syntax: function add(a, b) { return a + b; }
  - Example: let result = add(10, 20); console.log(result);
- Arrays:
  - Syntax: let fruits = ["Apple", "Mango", "Orange"];
  - Access: console.log(fruits[0]);
- Objects:
  - Syntax: let student = { name: "John", age: 20 };
  - Access: console.log(student.name);
- Events:
  - JavaScript responds to user actions.
  - Example: <button onclick="showMessage()">Click Me</button>
- DOM (Document Object Model):
  - JavaScript can modify HTML elements dynamically.
  - Example: document.getElementById("demo").innerHTML = "Welcome";
- Advantages of JavaScript:
  - Easy to learn.
  - Fast execution in browsers.
  - Creates interactive web pages.
  - Reduces server load.
  - Supports modern web development.
